functions.name: array_list_new
functions.description: Allocates a new array_list with the default initial capacity (32 elements). Deprecated in favor of array_list_new2(), which allows specifying an initial size. Pass an optional element-free callback to have elements freed when the list is destroyed or elements are removed.
requirements: free_fn may be NULL to indicate that elements are not automatically freed.
If provided, free_fn must be safe to call on each stored element pointer.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL before use (allocation may fail).
Do not rely on this function long-term; prefer array_list_new2() as this API is marked @deprecated.

functions.name: array_list_new2
functions.description: Allocates a new array_list with a caller-specified initial capacity. Intended for sizing the list close to the expected number of elements to reduce reallocations; excess capacity can later be reduced via array_list_shrink().
requirements: free_fn may be NULL to indicate that elements are not automatically freed.
If provided, free_fn must be safe to call on each stored element pointer.
initial_size should be chosen to closely match the expected element count (per doc comment).
initial_size must be non-negative (type is int; negative sizes are invalid).
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL before use (allocation may fail).

functions.name: array_list_free
functions.description: Destroys an array_list and releases all associated memory. If a free_fn was supplied at creation, it will be invoked for each stored element before the container itself is freed.
requirements: al may be NULL only if the implementation explicitly allows it; otherwise must be a valid array_list pointer returned by array_list_new/new2.
All pointers stored in the list must be valid for the provided free_fn if one was specified.
After calling, the array_list pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: array_list_get_idx
functions.description: Returns the element pointer stored at index i within the array_list.
requirements: al must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
i must be within the current bounds of the list (i < array_list_length(al)); out-of-range access is invalid/undefined.
Returned pointer is the stored element (may be NULL if a NULL element was stored).

functions.name: array_list_insert_idx
functions.signature: extern int array_list_insert_idx(struct array_list *al, size_t i, void *data);
functions.description: Inserts a new element at index i, shifting existing elements at and after i to the right to make room. May grow the underlying storage if needed.
requirements: al must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
i must be within 0..array_list_length(al) to insert at or before current end; inserting beyond current length is invalid unless implementation allows sparse growth (not documented).
data is stored as-is; if a free_fn is associated with the list, it must be safe to call on this pointer when removed/freed.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).

functions.name: array_list_put_idx
functions.signature: extern int array_list_put_idx(struct array_list *al, size_t i, void *data);
functions.description: Sets/replaces the element at index i. Implementations of json-c typically expand the list to accommodate larger indices, filling gaps as needed, but this header does not specify behavior; treat as setting an element at i.
requirements: al must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
i must be a valid index; if expansion is not supported by the implementation, i must be < current length (behavior not specified here).
If replacing an existing element, the list may call free_fn on the old element (implementation-dependent). Ensure old element pointers are compatible with free_fn if one is set.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).

functions.name: array_list_add
functions.description: Appends an element to the end of the array_list, growing the underlying storage if necessary.
requirements: al must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
data is stored as-is; if a free_fn is associated with the list, it must be safe to call on this pointer when removed/freed.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).

functions.name: array_list_length
functions.description: Returns the current number of elements stored in the array_list.
requirements: al must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.

functions.name: array_list_sort
functions.signature: extern void array_list_sort(struct array_list *arr, int (*compar)(const void *, const void *));
functions.description: Sorts the elements of arr in-place using the provided comparator, analogous to qsort. The comparator receives pointers to elements and must define a strict weak ordering.
requirements: arr must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
compar must be a valid function pointer and must be consistent with the elements stored (it must be able to compare two stored element pointers).
compar must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero to indicate ordering (qsort-style convention inferred from the signature).
Elements must be mutually comparable under compar; undefined behavior if not.

functions.name: array_list_bsearch
functions.signature: extern void *array_list_bsearch(const void **key, struct array_list *arr, int (*compar)(const void *, const void *));
functions.description: Performs a binary search for key within arr using the provided comparator, returning the matching element pointer if found, otherwise NULL. Intended to be used with arrays previously sorted by the same comparator.
requirements: key must be a non-NULL pointer to a key value compatible with compar.
arr must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
compar must be a valid function pointer and must be the same relation used to sort the array (comparator consistency is required for binary search).
arr should be sorted with compar prior to calling, otherwise result is undefined.
Returned pointer is the stored element or NULL if not found.

functions.name: array_list_del_idx
functions.signature: extern int array_list_del_idx(struct array_list *arr, size_t idx, size_t count);
functions.description: Deletes count elements starting at index idx, shifting subsequent elements left to fill the gap. May call the list's free_fn on each removed element.
requirements: arr must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
idx must be within current bounds and idx + count must not exceed array_list_length(arr); removing beyond the end is invalid/undefined.
If a free_fn was provided, it must be safe to call on each removed element.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).

functions.name: array_list_shrink
functions.signature: extern int array_list_shrink(struct array_list *arr, size_t empty_slots);
functions.description: Reduces the capacity of the array_list to fit exactly the current number of elements plus empty_slots, potentially freeing unused memory.
requirements: arr must be a valid, initialized array_list pointer.
empty_slots must be the desired number of extra capacity slots to keep; it must be a representable size_t value.
Caller must check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact semantics not documented here).

functions.name: mc_set_debug
functions.description: Enable or disable json-c’s internal debug logging. Intended for internal/maintainer use; the API may change or be removed. Typical usage is to pass 0 to disable and a non-zero value to enable debug output.
requirements: This is an internal API; external callers should not rely on its stability (may change or be removed at any time).
Argument debug is an integer flag; by convention, 0 disables and non-zero enables debug logging (inferred from naming and common patterns).

functions.description: Gets the current internal debug-logging level for json-c internals. In builds with MC_MAINTAINER_MODE defined, this macro calls mc_get_debug() and returns its result; otherwise it expands to the constant 0.
requirements: Only returns the actual debug level when MC_MAINTAINER_MODE is defined; otherwise always returns 0.

functions.description: Configures whether logging should use syslog for json-c internal messages. In builds with MC_MAINTAINER_MODE defined, this macro invokes mc_set_syslog(syslog); otherwise it expands to a no-op.
requirements: Only meaningful when compiled with MC_MAINTAINER_MODE defined; otherwise it does nothing.
Argument syslog is an integer flag; exact accepted values/semantics are not documented (unknown).
Caller should not rely on side effects when MC_MAINTAINER_MODE is not defined.

The first argument must be a valid printf-style format string; the variadic arguments must match the format specifiers.
fmt must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: json_c_version
functions.description: Returns the json-c library version as a read-only C string. Intended for runtime detection/diagnostics and to compare against compile-time expectations. The string corresponds to the JSON_C_VERSION macro (e.g., "0.18.99").
requirements: May be called at any time after the library is loaded; no initialization or state is required (inferred from having no parameters and being a pure query).
The returned pointer refers to a read-only, null-terminated string; the caller must not modify or free it (inferred from the const char* return type and common C API patterns).
No error conditions are documented; behavior of a NULL return is unspecified.

functions.name: json_c_version_num
functions.description: Returns the json-c library version encoded as an int, matching JSON_C_VERSION_NUM. Encoding: low 8 bits = micro, next 8 bits = minor, next 8 bits = major (e.g., 7.12.99 => 0x00070B63). Useful for numeric comparisons at runtime.
requirements: May be called at any time after the library is loaded; no initialization or state is required (inferred from having no parameters and being a pure query).
No error conditions are documented.

functions.name: json_object_get
functions.description: Increment the reference count of a json_object and return the same pointer. Use when you need to retain ownership beyond the parent’s lifetime or share across components/threads that will call json_object_put().
requirements: obj may be NULL; behavior is to return NULL and perform no change (inferred typical behavior, not explicitly stated).
Call json_object_put() once for each successful ownership you take via json_object_get().
Use when retaining a child beyond its parent’s lifetime, or when sharing across threads that will each eventually json_object_put().

functions.name: json_object_put
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of a json_object, freeing it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: Caller must have ownership of obj before calling, otherwise refcount imbalance may cause use-after-free.
Do not use obj after calling json_object_put() on it (or on any parent containing it) unless you incremented its refcount separately via json_object_get().
It is legal to pass NULL; this is a no-op.
Returns 1 if object was freed, 0 if only the refcount was decremented.

functions.name: json_object_is_type
functions.signature: int json_object_is_type(const struct json_object *obj, enum json_type type);
functions.description: Return whether the json_object is of the specified json_type.
requirements: type must be one of: json_type_null (obj == NULL), json_type_boolean, json_type_double, json_type_int, json_type_object, json_type_array, json_type_string.

functions.name: json_object_get_type
functions.description: Return the json_type of the given json_object. Use json_type_to_name() (elsewhere) to log a readable string.
requirements: obj may be NULL; returns json_type_null in that case.

functions.name: json_object_to_json_string
functions.description: Serialize a json_object to a JSON string with spaced formatting (equivalent to json_object_to_json_string_ext(obj, JSON_C_TO_STRING_SPACED)). The returned pointer is managed by the object; do not free.
requirements: Do not free the returned string; it is owned by the json_object.
If there may be concurrent access to obj, copy the string (e.g., via strdup()) before releasing locks or modifying the object.
Later json_object_put() of obj will release the internal string as needed.

functions.name: json_object_to_json_string_ext
functions.description: Serialize a json_object to a JSON string with formatting options specified by flags (e.g., JSON_C_TO_STRING_PRETTY, JSON_C_TO_STRING_SPACED, etc.). Returned pointer is owned by the object.
requirements: flags is a bitmask of JSON_C_TO_STRING_* constants.
Do not free the returned string; copy if needed for longer lifetime or thread safety.
obj must be a valid json_object; if NULL behavior is unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: json_object_to_json_string_length
functions.signature: const char *json_object_to_json_string_length(struct json_object *obj, int flags, size_t *length);
functions.description: Serialize a json_object to a JSON string with formatting options and optionally return its length (excluding the terminating null). Returned pointer is owned by the object.
requirements: flags is a bitmask of JSON_C_TO_STRING_* constants.
If length is non-NULL, the function stores the byte length excluding the null terminator.
Do not free the returned string; copy if needed for longer lifetime or thread safety.

functions.name: json_object_get_userdata
functions.description: Return the userdata pointer previously set on a json_object via json_object_set_userdata() or json_object_set_serializer().
requirements: jso must be a valid json_object; returns NULL if none set.

functions.name: json_object_set_userdata
functions.description: Associate an opaque userdata pointer with a json_object. Optionally set a function to be called to free the userdata when the object is deleted.
requirements: If custom userdata was already set, any existing user_delete will be called before replacing it.
user_delete may be NULL even if userdata is non-NULL; in that case caller is responsible for freeing userdata at an appropriate time (after object deletion).
The delete callback (if set) is called just before the object is deleted (when refcount reaches zero).
For objects created by parsing (that may have custom serializers expecting userdata), prefer json_object_set_serializer(jso, NULL, userdata, user_delete) to reset serializer and set userdata.

functions.name: json_object_set_serializer
functions.description: Set a custom serialization function for a specific json_object, along with optional userdata and an optional delete callback. Passing to_string_func as NULL resets to default serializer (userdata/delete remain set).
requirements: If existing userdata is set, its prior user_delete (if any) will be called before replacing.
userdata may be NULL, even if user_delete is non-NULL.
user_delete may be NULL even if userdata is non-NULL; then caller must free userdata later (after deletion).
Note the userdata set here is the same slot used by json_object_set_userdata(); avoid unintended overwrite when using both.

functions.name: json_object_free_userdata
functions.description: Utility delete function that simply calls free(userdata). Intended for use as user_delete with json_object_set_serializer() or json_object_set_userdata().
requirements: userdata must point to memory allocated with compatible allocator for free().
jso is unused.

functions.name: json_object_userdata_to_json_string

functions.name: json_object_new_object
functions.description: Create a new empty object of type json_type_object with refcount 1. Caller initially owns it.

functions.name: json_object_get_object
functions.description: Return the underlying linkhash table for an object of type json_type_object.
requirements: obj must be a json_type_object; otherwise returned value is undefined here (unknown).

functions.name: json_object_object_length

requirements: obj must be a json_type_object.

functions.name: json_c_object_sizeof
functions.description: Return sizeof(struct json_object). Useful for ABI verification or memory accounting.

functions.name: json_object_object_add
functions.signature: int json_object_object_add(struct json_object *obj, const char *key, struct json_object *val);

key is duplicated internally (private copy).

functions.name: json_object_object_add_ex
functions.signature: int json_object_object_add_ex(struct json_object *obj, const char *const key, struct json_object *const val, const unsigned opts);

functions.name: json_object_object_get
functions.signature: struct json_object *json_object_object_get(const struct json_object *obj, const char *key);
functions.description: Deprecated helper to fetch the value for a key from an object. Returns NULL if the key does not exist, the value is null, or obj is not an object. Does not change refcounts.
requirements: Prefer json_object_object_get_ex() for distinguishing missing vs null.

functions.name: json_object_object_get_ex
functions.signature: int json_object_object_get_ex(const struct json_object *obj, const char *key, struct json_object **value);
functions.description: Lookup a key in an object. If found, optionally stores the value in *value, and returns 1; otherwise returns 0. Does not change refcounts.
requirements: obj should be json_type_object; otherwise returns 0.
It is safe to pass value as NULL.
Ownership of any returned value remains with obj; json_object_get() if you need to keep it beyond obj’s lifetime.

functions.name: json_object_object_del
functions.description: Delete a field from an object. Decrements the reference count of the removed value; it may be freed if no longer referenced.
requirements: obj must be json_type_object.

functions.name: json_object_new_array
functions.description: Create a new empty array object (json_type_array) with 32 slots preallocated. Refcount is 1; caller owns initially.

functions.name: json_object_new_array_ext

functions.name: json_object_get_array
functions.description: Return the internal array_list of a json_type_array.

functions.name: json_object_array_length

requirements: obj must be a json_type_array.

functions.name: json_object_array_sort
functions.signature: void json_object_array_sort(struct json_object *jso, int (*sort_fn)(const void *, const void *));

functions.description: Binary search a sorted array for a specified key object using the provided comparator. Returns the matching json_object or NULL if not found.

functions.name: json_object_array_add
functions.description: Append an element to the end of an array. Ownership of val transfers to the array; its refcount is not incremented.
requirements: obj must be a json_type_array.

functions.name: json_object_array_put_idx

idx is zero-based.
If you need to retain a reference to val, call json_object_get(val) before passing.

functions.name: json_object_array_insert_idx
functions.signature: int json_object_array_insert_idx(struct json_object *obj, size_t idx, struct json_object *val);
functions.description: Insert an element at the specified index, shifting existing elements to the right if within bounds. Expands the array if idx is beyond current size. Ownership of val transfers to the array.
requirements: obj must be a json_type_array.
idx is zero-based.
If idx <= length, existing elements at idx..end are shifted right by one.
If you need to retain a reference to val, call json_object_get(val) first.

functions.name: json_object_array_get_idx
functions.signature: struct json_object *json_object_array_get_idx(const struct json_object *obj, size_t idx);
functions.description: Return the element at the specified index of an array. Does not change refcounts; ownership remains with the array.
requirements: obj must be a json_type_array; calling with other types triggers an assert.
idx is zero-based; returns NULL if out of range.

functions.name: json_object_array_del_idx
functions.signature: int json_object_array_del_idx(struct json_object *obj, size_t idx, size_t count);
functions.description: Delete count elements starting at index idx from an array. Decrements refcount of each removed element and frees them if no longer referenced.
requirements: obj must be a json_type_array.
idx is zero-based; elements beyond bounds are ignored (exact behavior on out-of-range count not further specified).
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: json_object_array_shrink
functions.description: Reduce the array’s internal allocation to fit its current element count plus empty_slots spare capacity.
requirements: jso must be json_type_array.
empty_slots specifies additional free slots to leave allocated.
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: json_object_new_boolean
functions.description: Create a new boolean json_object with value b (0 or 1).
requirements: b must be 0 or 1 (json_bool).

functions.name: json_object_get_boolean
functions.description: Return the boolean value of a json_object, coercing from other types per documented rules (numbers: 0 -> 0, non-zero -> 1; strings: non-empty -> 1; arrays/objects -> 0).
requirements: If obj is not a boolean, coercion rules apply as documented; for non-boolean non-string/number types returns 0.
If obj is NULL (json_type_null), returns 0 without error flags.

functions.name: json_object_set_boolean
functions.description: Set the value of a boolean json_object.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_boolean; otherwise returns 0 and makes no changes.
new_value should be 0 or 1.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_new_int
functions.description: Create a new integer json_object (stored internally as 64-bit). For full 64-bit range use json_object_new_int64().

functions.name: json_object_new_int64
functions.description: Create a new 64-bit integer json_object.

functions.name: json_object_new_uint64
functions.description: Create a new unsigned 64-bit integer json_object.

functions.name: json_object_get_int
functions.description: Return the 32-bit integer value of a json_object, coercing from other types per documented rules. Sets errno on errors or range issues.
requirements: If obj is a double NaN -> returns INT32_MIN and sets errno=EINVAL.
If obj is a string and not convertible -> returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL.
If value out of int32 range -> sets errno=ERANGE and returns INT32_MAX/INT32_MIN for overflow/underflow.
If obj is NULL -> returns 0 (no errno set).
Integers stored internally as 64-bit are clamped to 32-bit as needed.

functions.name: json_object_set_int
functions.description: Set the value of an integer json_object (json_type_int) to new_value.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_int; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_int_inc
functions.description: Increment (or decrement if negative) an integer json_object by val. On overflow sets value to INT64_MAX; on underflow sets to INT64_MIN.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_int; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
Overflow/underflow do not affect return value; result is clamped accordingly.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_get_int64
functions.description: Return the 64-bit integer value of a json_object, coercing from other types. Sets errno on errors or range issues. Caller should set errno=0 before the call to detect errors.
requirements: If obj is a double NaN -> returns INT64_MIN and sets errno=EINVAL.
If obj is a string and not convertible -> returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL.
If value out of int64 range -> sets errno=ERANGE.
If obj is NULL -> returns 0 (no errno set).
Caller should set errno to 0 before calling to disambiguate success from failure.

functions.name: json_object_get_uint64
functions.description: Return the unsigned 64-bit integer value of a json_object, coercing from other types. Sets errno on errors or range issues. Caller should set errno=0 before the call to detect errors.
requirements: If obj is a double NaN -> returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL.
If obj is a string and not convertible -> returns 0 and sets errno=EINVAL.
If value out of uint64 range -> sets errno=ERANGE.
If obj is NULL -> returns 0 (no errno set).
Caller should set errno to 0 before calling to disambiguate success from failure.

functions.name: json_object_set_int64
functions.description: Set the value of an integer json_object (json_type_int) to the specified 64-bit value.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_int; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_set_uint64
functions.description: Set the value of an unsigned integer json_object (json_type_uint) to the specified 64-bit value.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_uint; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_new_double
functions.description: Create a new double json_object with value d. Default serialization uses a configurable printf format (see json_c_set_serialization_double_format or json_object_set_serializer).

functions.name: json_object_new_double_s
functions.description: Create a new double json_object that preserves the exact string representation ds when serialized. Useful to avoid lossy or verbose double formatting.
requirements: ds is copied; it should be a valid string representation of d for consistent behavior.
This uses the object’s userdata to store ds; that userdata slot is not available for other uses unless serializer is reset.

functions.name: json_c_set_serialization_double_format
functions.description: Set the printf-style format used to serialize doubles, either globally or thread-locally. The format should be a %g-style format string (e.g., "%.17g").
requirements: double_format must be a valid printf %g format string.
global_or_thread must be JSON_C_OPTION_GLOBAL or JSON_C_OPTION_THREAD.
Setting thread-local options requires json-c to be compiled with threading and thread-local storage; otherwise returns -1.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: json_object_double_to_json_string
functions.signature: int json_object_double_to_json_string(struct json_object *jso, struct printbuf *pb, int level, int flags);
functions.description: Serializer callback for json_type_double objects; writes the serialized representation to pb using the current double format settings.
requirements: Normally used via json_object_set_serializer(); not intended for direct use in most code.
level and flags are ignored.
jso must be json_type_double.
pb must be a valid printbuf.

functions.name: json_object_get_double
functions.description: Return the double value of a json_object, coercing from other types per documented rules. Sets errno on errors: ERANGE for overflow to infinity; EINVAL for invalid conversion resulting in NaN.
requirements: If obj is NULL -> returns 0.0 (no errno set).
Arrays: length 0 -> 0 (no error); length 1 -> cast that element; other lengths -> set errno=EINVAL and return NaN.
Caller should set errno=0 before calling to detect errors (recommended).

functions.name: json_object_set_double
functions.description: Set the value of a double json_object. If the object was created with json_object_new_double_s(), resets serializer to default and clears cached serialized value.
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_double; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_new_string
functions.description: Create a new string json_object by copying the zero-terminated input string. Memory is managed by the json_object.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a string (copied on creation).

functions.name: json_object_new_string_len
functions.signature: struct json_object *json_object_new_string_len(const char *s, const int len);
functions.description: Create a new string json_object copying exactly len bytes from s (need not be NUL-terminated).
requirements: s must point to at least len bytes.
len specifies the maximum bytes to copy.

functions.name: json_object_get_string
functions.description: Return a const char* view of the string value if obj is a string; otherwise return the JSON representation of obj as a string. The memory is owned by the json_object.
requirements: If obj is of type json_type_null (obj == NULL), returns NULL.
Do not free or modify the returned string; copy if needed beyond the object’s lifetime or for thread safety.

functions.name: json_object_get_string_len
functions.description: Return the string length if obj is a json_type_string; otherwise return 0.

functions.name: json_object_set_string
functions.description: Set the value of a string json_object using a NUL-terminated string. Equivalent to json_object_set_string_len(obj, new_value, strlen(new_value)).
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_string; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
new_value must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_set_string_len
functions.signature: int json_object_set_string_len(json_object *obj, const char *new_value, int len);
functions.description: Set the value of a string json_object using exactly len bytes from new_value (need not be NUL-terminated).
requirements: obj must be of type json_type_string; otherwise returns 0 without changes.
new_value must point to at least len bytes.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_object_new_null
functions.description: Placeholder function to mirror json_object_new_* API; always returns NULL. It is acceptable to use NULL directly.

functions.name: json_object_equal
functions.description: Check for deep equality between two json_objects. Compares by type and value; arrays require same order; objects require all keys equal regardless of order.
requirements: Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: json_c_shallow_copy_default
functions.signature: int json_c_shallow_copy_default(json_object *src, json_object *parent, const char *key, size_t index, json_object **dst);
functions.description: Default shallow copy routine used by json_object_deep_copy(). Creates a new object of the same type and copies the serializer function (but not userdata/user_delete).
requirements: src is never NULL.
If src is within a container, parent and either key or index are provided (may be NULL otherwise).
On entry, *dst must be NULL; function must set *dst to non-NULL on success.
Returns 1 on success, -1 on error; never returns 2.

functions.name: json_object_deep_copy
functions.signature: int json_object_deep_copy(struct json_object *src, struct json_object **dst, json_c_shallow_copy_fn *shallow_copy);
functions.description: Perform a deep copy of src into *dst, optionally using a custom shallow_copy for individual objects (useful if custom serializers are in use). Equivalent in effect to parsing the serialization of src.
requirements: dst must point to a variable initialized to NULL; function returns -1 if *dst is non-NULL.
src must be a valid json_object.
If shallow_copy is provided, it must follow json_c_shallow_copy_fn contract and may return 2 to indicate custom serializer handling.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: json_object_iter_init_default
functions.description: Initialize and return a default/invalid json_object_iterator value. This is useful for initializing iterator variables (e.g., in a constructor initializer list). The returned iterator does not reference any pair and must not be used with other iterator APIs until it is assigned a valid iterator (e.g., from json_object_iter_begin or json_object_iter_end).
requirements: Returned iterator is invalid by design and MUST NOT be passed to APIs that expect a valid, non-end iterator.
This API (and iterator operations) are not thread-safe or reentrant; synchronize externally when accessing the same JSON object from multiple threads.

functions.name: json_object_iter_begin
functions.description: Return an iterator positioned at the first name/value pair of the given JSON Object. If the object has no pairs, the returned iterator is equal to the corresponding end iterator for that object.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to a json-c JSON Object instance (i.e., of type object).
Any modification of the underlying object’s pairs invalidates all iterators to those pairs.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; callers must provide external synchronization if the object can be modified/read concurrently.
To iterate, compare against the end iterator obtained from the same object using json_object_iter_end(obj).

functions.name: json_object_iter_end
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT struct json_object_iterator json_object_iter_end(const struct json_object *obj)
functions.description: Return the end iterator for the given JSON Object, representing the position one past the last pair. Used as a sentinel for iteration termination.
requirements: obj must be a valid pointer to a json-c JSON Object instance (i.e., of type object).
Do not assume the end iterator has a NULL internal value; only compare using json_object_iter_equal with iterators derived from the same object.
For performance, obtain and store the end iterator before looping.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; callers must synchronize concurrent access/modification.

functions.name: json_object_iter_next
functions.description: Advance the given iterator to the next name/value pair in the same JSON Object, or to the end iterator if there are no more pairs.
requirements: iter must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, non-end iterator.
Passing an invalid or end iterator results in undefined/bad behavior.
On return, iter refers to the next pair if one exists, otherwise to the object’s end iterator (comparable to json_object_iter_end() for that object).
Any modification of the underlying pair invalidates all iterators to that pair.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; synchronize externally if the object may be accessed concurrently.

functions.name: json_object_iter_peek_name
functions.description: Return a const pointer to the key (name) of the name/value pair referenced by the iterator. The returned pointer is owned by the object and remains valid until the pair is deleted or modified.
requirements: iter must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, non-end iterator.
Do not modify or free the returned string pointer; its lifetime is tied to the underlying pair and ends when the pair is deleted or modified.
Passing an invalid or end iterator results in undefined/bad behavior.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; external synchronization required for concurrent access.

functions.name: json_object_iter_peek_value
functions.description: Return a pointer to the json_object value of the name/value pair referenced by the iterator without changing its reference count. May return NULL to represent a JSON null value.
requirements: iter must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, non-end iterator.
The returned json_object pointer is not refcounted by this call; if the caller needs to retain it beyond the iterator’s validity, call json_object_get() and later json_object_put().
JSON null values are represented as a NULL json_object pointer; callers must handle NULL appropriately.
Passing an invalid or end iterator results in undefined/bad behavior.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; synchronize externally if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: json_object_iter_equal
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT json_bool json_object_iter_equal(const struct json_object_iterator *iter1, const struct json_object_iterator *iter2)
functions.description: Compare two iterators for equality. Returns non-zero if both reference the same pair or both are end iterators for the same JSON Object instance; otherwise returns zero. Typically used to detect end of iteration.
requirements: iter1 and iter2 must be non-NULL pointers to valid iterators derived from the same JSON Object instance.
Passing NULL, uninitialized/invalid iterators, or iterators from different JSON Object instances leads to undefined/bad behavior.
Not thread-safe or reentrant; concurrent access requires external synchronization.

functions.name: json_tokener_get_parse_end
functions.description: Return the byte offset (relative to the most recent input string passed to json_tokener_parse_ex) of the first unparsed byte. Useful for continuing parsing after a successfully parsed JSON value or detecting trailing characters.
requirements: tok must point to a valid json_tokener previously used with json_tokener_parse_ex().
This value is relative to the start of the most recent string passed to json_tokener_parse_ex(), not a cumulative count over multiple calls.

functions.name: json_tokener_error_desc
functions.description: Return a human-readable description string for a json_tokener_error code. If an invalid error code is provided, a generic error message is returned.
requirements: jerr should be a value from enum json_tokener_error; invalid values will yield a generic message.

functions.name: json_tokener_get_error
functions.description: Retrieve the error status from the last call to json_tokener_parse_ex for this tokener. Returns json_tokener_success if there is no error; returns json_tokener_continue if parsing is in progress over partial input.
requirements: tok must point to a valid json_tokener.
Call after json_tokener_parse_ex() to check status; json_tokener_continue indicates more data is required before parsing can complete.

functions.name: json_tokener_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new json_tokener instance for parsing JSON input. Free it with json_tokener_free() when done.
requirements: Caller must free the returned tokener with json_tokener_free() when no longer needed.
The returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure (implied by general C allocation patterns; specific behavior not detailed).

functions.name: json_tokener_new_ex
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new json_tokener with a specified maximum nesting depth.
requirements: depth must be at least 1.
Caller must free the returned tokener with json_tokener_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_tokener_free
functions.description: Free a json_tokener previously allocated with json_tokener_new() or json_tokener_new_ex().
requirements: tok must have been allocated by json_tokener_new() or json_tokener_new_ex().
Do not use tok after this call.

functions.name: json_tokener_reset
functions.description: Reset a json_tokener’s internal state so it can parse a brand new JSON value after a completed or failed parse.
requirements: tok must be a valid json_tokener instance.
Must be called before reusing tok if json_tokener_parse_ex() returned NULL with an error other than json_tokener_continue.

functions.name: json_tokener_parse
functions.description: Parse an entire JSON text from a C string and return the resulting json_object. This is a convenience wrapper around json_tokener_parse_ex() for simple, complete inputs.
requirements: str should point to a valid JSON text. The function expects a complete input string (implied by being a simple wrapper).
On success, the returned json_object has a reference count of one and belongs to the caller (as with parse_ex); check the type with json_object_is_type() or json_object_get_type() before use.

functions.name: json_tokener_parse_verbose
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT struct json_object *json_tokener_parse_verbose(const char *str, enum json_tokener_error *error);
functions.description: Parse a JSON text from a C string, returning the parsed json_object on success; on failure, write the error code to *error. Provides error reporting convenience over json_tokener_parse().
requirements: str should point to a valid C string containing JSON text.
error should be a valid pointer to enum json_tokener_error storage to receive the error code if parsing fails; behavior if NULL is not specified in the header.
On success, the returned json_object has a reference count of one and belongs to the caller.

functions.name: json_tokener_set_flags
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT void json_tokener_set_flags(struct json_tokener *tok, int flags);
functions.description: Set parsing behavior flags for a json_tokener. Supported flags include JSON_TOKENER_STRICT (be strict about valid input), JSON_TOKENER_ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS (allow extra characters after the first parsed value when combined with STRICT), and JSON_TOKENER_VALIDATE_UTF8 (validate that input is UTF-8, causing json_tokener_error_parse_utf8_string on failure).
requirements: tok must be a valid json_tokener.
flags is a bitmask composed of JSON_TOKENER_* macros defined in this header.
Using JSON_TOKENER_STRICT disables parsing multiple JSON values from a single character stream unless JSON_TOKENER_ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS is also set.

functions.name: json_tokener_parse_ex
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT struct json_object *json_tokener_parse_ex(struct json_tokener *tok, const char *str, int len);
functions.description: Incrementally parse a JSON value from a byte buffer. Returns a json_object on success; returns NULL if more data is needed (json_tokener_continue) or on fatal error. Supports parsing complete values of any JSON type (object, array, string, number, boolean, null) and allows feeding input in chunks.
requirements: tok must be a json_tokener allocated by json_tokener_new()/json_tokener_new_ex().
str points to a buffer containing JSON data; it does not need to be NUL-terminated.

len is the number of bytes available at str; if the caller knows this is the end of input, len MUST include the final '\0' so values without inherent terminators (e.g., numbers) can finish parsing instead of returning json_tokener_continue.
If the function returns NULL and json_tokener_get_error(tok) != json_tokener_continue, a fatal error occurred; do not reuse tok until json_tokener_reset() is called.
To detect extra characters after the parsed value, compare json_tokener_get_parse_end(tok) to the len value passed for the last call.

The tokener does not maintain an internal buffer; for subsequent calls, the caller must pass str pointing at any remaining (unparsed) characters starting at the offset indicated by json_tokener_get_parse_end().
The maximum accepted string size is limited to INT32_MAX (2GB) due to the int len parameter. If len == -1, strlen() is used and the string length must be < INT32_MAX.
When JSON_TOKENER_VALIDATE_UTF8 is set via json_tokener_set_flags(), input must be valid UTF-8 or json_tokener_get_error(tok) will be json_tokener_error_parse_utf8_string.
On success, the returned json_object has a reference count of one; check its type with json_object_is_type() or json_object_get_type() before use.

functions.name: json_object_from_file
functions.description: Read the entire contents of a file and parse it into a json_object using json_tokener_parse(). Returns NULL on failure; details can be retrieved with json_util_get_last_err(). Typical usage: pass a path to a file containing a complete JSON document to obtain a json_object.
requirements: filename must reference a readable file containing valid JSON text.
On failure, callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.
The returned json_object must be released according to json-c ownership rules (e.g., json_object_put())

functions.name: json_object_from_fd_ex
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT struct json_object *json_object_from_fd_ex(int fd, int depth);
functions.description: Parse JSON from an already-open file descriptor into a json_object, using a specified maximum parse depth. When depth is -1, JSON_TOKENER_DEFAULT_DEPTH is used. Returns NULL on failure; see json_util_get_last_err() for details.
requirements: fd must be open and readable at the current file position.
If the JSON content is at the beginning of the file, use lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) before calling to ensure reading starts at the beginning.
depth must be -1 to use the default, otherwise it should be a non-negative maximum object depth expected by json_tokener_new_ex().
On failure, callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.
The returned json_object must be released according to json-c ownership rules (e.g., json_object_put())

functions.name: json_object_from_fd
functions.description: Parse JSON from an already-open file descriptor into a json_object using the default maximum object depth (JSON_TOKENER_DEFAULT_DEPTH). Returns NULL on failure; see json_util_get_last_err() for details.
requirements: fd must be open and readable at the current file position.
If the JSON content is at the beginning of the file, use lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET) before calling.
On failure, callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.
The returned json_object must be released according to json-c ownership rules (e.g., json_object_put())

functions.name: json_object_to_file
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_object_to_file(const char *filename, struct json_object *obj);
functions.description: Write a json_object to a file as JSON text. Equivalent to calling json_object_to_file_ext(filename, obj, JSON_C_TO_STRING_PLAIN). Returns -1 on failure; details can be retrieved with json_util_get_last_err().
requirements: filename must be a writable path; the function opens and truncates the file, creating it if necessary (via its equivalent ext call).
obj must be a valid pointer to a json_object.
On failure (return -1), callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.

functions.name: json_object_to_file_ext
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_object_to_file_ext(const char *filename, struct json_object *obj, int flags);
functions.description: Open (creating if necessary) and truncate the given file, convert the json_object to a string, and write it to the file using the specified serialization flags. Returns -1 on failure; see json_util_get_last_err() for details.
requirements: filename must be a writable path; the file will be created if it does not exist and truncated if it does.
obj must be a valid pointer to a json_object.
flags are passed to json_object_to_json_string_ext(); use values defined by json-c (e.g., JSON_C_TO_STRING_*).
On failure (return -1), callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.

functions.name: json_object_to_fd
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_object_to_fd(int fd, struct json_object *obj, int flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_object to JSON text and write it to an open file descriptor. The function handles partial writes and continues until all data is written or an error occurs. Returns -1 on failure; see json_util_get_last_err() for details.
requirements: fd must be open and writable.
obj must be a valid pointer to a json_object.
flags are passed to json_object_to_json_string_ext(); use values defined by json-c (e.g., JSON_C_TO_STRING_*).
On failure (return -1), callers should check json_util_get_last_err() for a diagnostic message.

functions.name: json_util_get_last_err
functions.description: Return a pointer to a message string describing the most recent error from various json-c functions (e.g., json_object_to_file, json_object_to_file_ext, json_object_to_fd, json_object_from_file, json_object_from_fd), or NULL if no error is recorded.
requirements: The returned pointer, if non-NULL, refers to memory managed by the library; callers must not modify or free it.
Call this after a function reports failure to obtain a diagnostic message.

functions.name: json_parse_int64
functions.description: Parse a decimal integer from a NUL-terminated string into a 64-bit signed integer. Returns 0 on success and stores the result in *retval. Overflow/underflow are not treated as errors, but errno will be set to ERANGE (mimicking strtol/strtoll behavior).
requirements: buf must point to a NUL-terminated string representation of an integer.
retval must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed value.
On overflow/underflow, callers should check errno for ERANGE if needed; function still returns 0 on successful parse of magnitude.
Non-zero return indicates failure to parse (exact failure modes not documented here).

functions.name: json_parse_uint64
functions.description: Parse an unsigned integer from a NUL-terminated string into a 64-bit unsigned integer, with one extra bit of magnitude allowed beyond json_parse_int64(). Returns 0 on success and stores the result in *retval. Other detailed behaviors are not documented here.
requirements: buf must point to a NUL-terminated string representation of a non-negative integer.
retval must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed value.
Behavior on overflow/underflow and errno settings are not specified in this header; callers should treat values outside uint64_t range as resulting in implementation-defined error handling.
Non-zero return indicates failure to parse (exact failure modes not documented here).

functions.name: json_parse_double
functions.description: [Deprecated] Parse a floating-point number from a NUL-terminated string into a double. Returns an int status (0 on success is implied by convention, but not explicitly documented here). Prefer alternative parsing where available. Specific error reporting is not documented in this header.
requirements: buf should point to a NUL-terminated string containing a floating-point representation.
retval must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed value.
As deprecated, new code should avoid using this function; if used, handle non-zero return as a parse failure.

functions.name: json_type_to_name
functions.description: Return a constant string describing the given json-c type, such as "int" or "object". Useful for diagnostics and logging.
requirements: o_type should be a valid value of enum json_type as defined by json-c.
The returned string is managed by the library and must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: json_c_visit
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_c_visit(json_object *jso, int future_flags, json_c_visit_userfunc *userfunc, void *userarg);
functions.description: Walks a JSON-C object tree depth-first starting at jso and invokes the user-supplied callback for each node. Containers (arrays and objects) are visited twice: once before iterating members and again after, with JSON_C_VISIT_SECOND set in flags on the second call. The callback receives the current node, flags, the parent (if any), and either the key (for object members) or index (for array elements). The callback must return one of the documented codes to control traversal: CONTINUE, SKIP, POP, STOP, or ERROR. Returns 0 if traversal completed without internal errors (even if nodes were intentionally skipped); returns <0 on error, including if the callback returns JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_ERROR. Intended for read/inspect or controlled traversal of a json_object hierarchy. Notes: the exact meaning/usage of future_flags is not documented here; treat it as reserved.
requirements: jso must be a valid pointer to a json_object that is the root of the traversal (inferred from signature and documentation wording).
userfunc must be a valid function pointer of type int(json_c_visit_userfunc)(json_object *jso, int flags, json_object *parent_jso, const char *jso_key, size_t *jso_index, void *userarg).

userfunc must return one of the defined return values: JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_CONTINUE, JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_SKIP, JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_POP, JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_STOP, or JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_ERROR (explicit).
userfunc must handle that for the root node parent_jso will be NULL (implied by “anything other than jso itself” having a parent).
userfunc must handle that exactly one of jso_key or jso_index is set for non-root nodes depending on whether the parent is an object (key set) or array (index set) (explicit).
userfunc must handle that flags may include JSON_C_VISIT_SECOND when a container is visited the second time after its children have been iterated (explicit).
Callers should pass 0 for future_flags; other values are reserved/unknown based on its name and lack of documentation (unknown specifics; recommended as 0).

Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates successful visitation (even with skips); a negative value indicates an error including when the callback returned JSON_C_VISIT_RETURN_ERROR (explicit).
userarg is an opaque pointer passed through to userfunc; whether NULL is acceptable is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: json_global_set_string_hash
functions.description: Sets the global string-hashing algorithm used by the library. Intended to be one of the JSON_C_STR_HASH_* constants (e.g., JSON_C_STR_HASH_DFLT, JSON_C_STR_HASH_PERLLIKE). Returns 0 on success, -1 if the parameter is invalid. Typical usage is to choose the hash policy once, then create/operate on tables or objects.
requirements: h must be one of the defined JSON_C_STR_HASH_* constants; otherwise the function returns -1.
Should be called with a valid integer value; behavior for other values is invalid.
Thread-safety and when it should be called are not documented; callers should assume global effect. Unknown details beyond this.

functions.name: lh_table_new
functions.signature: struct lh_table *lh_table_new(int size, lh_entry_free_fn *free_fn, lh_hash_fn *hash_fn, lh_equal_fn *equal_fn);
functions.description: Creates a new link-hash table with the specified initial size and callbacks. The free_fn (if non-NULL) is invoked on each entry when entries are deleted or the table is freed. hash_fn and equal_fn define the hashing and key comparison semantics. Returns a pointer to the new table on success, or NULL on error.
requirements: size is an initial table size; larger or smaller sizes affect performance and resizing but no specific range is documented.
If free_fn is NULL, the caller is responsible for freeing keys and values when entries are removed or the table is freed.
hash_fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with lh_hash_fn (unsigned long (*)(const void *)); usage elsewhere assumes it is non-NULL.
equal_fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with lh_equal_fn (int (*)(const void *, const void *)); usage elsewhere assumes it is non-NULL.
The returned table pointer must be freed with lh_table_free().

functions.name: lh_kchar_table_new
functions.description: Convenience constructor for a link-hash table keyed by C strings (char*). Internally configures string hashing and equality. Returns a new table on success, or NULL on error.
requirements: size is an initial table size; exact constraints are not documented.
If free_fn is NULL, the caller is responsible for freeing keys and values on deletion/free.
Returned table must be freed with lh_table_free().
Keys are expected to be C strings; exact lifetime/ownership depends on free_fn and insert options.

functions.name: lh_kptr_table_new
functions.description: Convenience constructor for a link-hash table keyed by pointer values. Returns a new table on success, or NULL on error.
requirements: size is an initial table size; exact constraints are not documented.
If free_fn is NULL, the caller is responsible for freeing keys and values on deletion/free.
Returned table must be freed with lh_table_free().
Keys are expected to be pointer values; equality and hashing are pointer-based.

functions.name: lh_table_free
functions.description: Frees a link-hash table. If a free function was supplied at construction, it is called for all entries before deallocating internal structures.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table* previously created by a corresponding constructor (e.g., lh_table_new/lh_kchar_table_new/lh_kptr_table_new).
If a free function was not provided, the caller must have already freed any dynamically allocated keys/values or accept that they won’t be freed here.
Do not use t after calling this function.

functions.name: lh_table_insert
functions.signature: int lh_table_insert(struct lh_table *t, const void *k, const void *v);
functions.description: Inserts a key/value pair into the table, resizing as needed. Returns 0 on success, a negative value on error.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table* created by a constructor and not yet freed.
k is a pointer to the key; its interpretation depends on the table’s hash/equal functions (e.g., C string for char-key tables).
v is a pointer to the value; ownership/lifetime interaction depends on the table’s free_fn and any insert options (unknown beyond that).
Behavior and constraints for NULL keys/values are not documented; callers should avoid NULL unless the configured hash/equal functions can handle them.

functions.name: lh_table_insert_w_hash
functions.signature: int lh_table_insert_w_hash(struct lh_table *t, const void *k, const void *v, const unsigned long h, const unsigned opts);
functions.description: Inserts a key/value pair using a caller-precomputed hash value for the key. This can optimize workflows performing multiple operations on the same key. If opts includes JSON_C_OBJECT_ADD_CONSTANT_KEY, the entry’s key is marked constant so the table’s free function will not free it. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
k must be the key for which the supplied hash h was computed; the header recommends calculating h via lh_get_hash(t, k).
h should be the hash of k as computed by the table’s hash function; passing mismatched hashes can cause lookup/insert anomalies.
opts may include JSON_C_OBJECT_ADD_CONSTANT_KEY to mark the key as constant; other option values are not documented here.
Value and key ownership/freeing behavior depends on the table’s free_fn and the constant-key flag.

functions.name: lh_table_lookup_entry
functions.description: Looks up a key and returns the corresponding entry structure, or NULL if not found. The returned lh_entry is part of the table; do not free it directly.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
k must be a key compatible with the table’s hash/equal functions.
The returned entry pointer, if non-NULL, remains owned by the table; it becomes invalid if the table is modified in ways that remove that entry or the table is freed.

functions.name: lh_table_lookup_entry_w_hash
functions.signature: struct lh_entry *lh_table_lookup_entry_w_hash(struct lh_table *t, const void *k, const unsigned long h);
functions.description: Looks up a key using a caller-provided hash value and returns the associated entry, or NULL if not found. Using a precomputed hash can optimize repeated operations on the same key.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
k must be the key corresponding to the supplied hash h (ideally calculated via lh_get_hash(t, k)).
The returned entry pointer, if non-NULL, is owned by the table and is invalidated by deletion or table free.

functions.name: lh_table_lookup_ex
functions.signature: json_bool lh_table_lookup_ex(struct lh_table *t, const void *k, void **v);
functions.description: Looks up a key and, if found, stores the associated value pointer in *v; otherwise sets *v to NULL. Returns a json_bool indicating whether the key was found.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
k must be a key compatible with the table’s hash/equal functions.
v must be a valid pointer to a void*; on return, *v is set to the found value or NULL if not found.

functions.name: lh_table_delete_entry
functions.description: Deletes the specified entry from the table. If a free function was provided, it is called for the entry being deleted. Returns 0 on success, -1 if not found.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
e must be a pointer to an entry that belongs to table t; deleting an entry from another table or a stale pointer yields undefined behavior.
After deletion, e must not be used.
If a free function was provided at table creation, it will be invoked for the deleted entry.

functions.name: lh_table_delete
functions.description: Deletes the entry associated with the given key. If a free function was provided, it is called for the deleted entry. Returns 0 if the item was deleted, -1 if not found.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
k must be a key compatible with the table’s hash/equal functions.
After deletion the entry is removed; any pointers obtained to that entry become invalid.

functions.name: lh_table_length
functions.description: Returns the number of entries currently stored in the table.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*. The function reads the table state; no additional constraints are documented.

functions.name: lh_table_resize
functions.description: Resizes the table to the specified new_size. Returns 0 on success, negative on error. Useful to pre-grow or shrink the table to reduce rehashing cost.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
new_size must be positive (explicitly documented).
Existing pointers to entries may become invalid after resize; callers should not rely on prior lh_entry pointers across a resize (not explicitly stated but typical; exercise caution).

functions.name: lh_table_head
functions.description: Returns the first entry (head) in the table’s insertion order, or NULL if the table is empty. Often used with lh_entry_next() to iterate.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table*.
The returned pointer is owned by the table; it becomes invalid if the entry is deleted or the table is freed.

functions.name: lh_get_hash
functions.signature: static inline unsigned long lh_get_hash(const struct lh_table *t, const void *k);
functions.description: Computes the hash for key k using the table’s configured hash function. Useful for cases where the hash is reused across multiple operations.
requirements: t must be a valid lh_table* with a valid, non-NULL hash_fn configured.
k must be a key acceptable to t’s hash function.

functions.name: lh_entry_k
functions.description: Returns a non-const pointer to the entry’s key. The key is stored as const internally to discourage modification by linkhash; callers may use the returned pointer at their own risk.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry.
Modifying the key memory can violate table invariants; the header notes only that linkhash itself doesn’t modify it. Use with care.

functions.name: lh_entry_k_is_constant
functions.signature: static inline int lh_entry_k_is_constant(const struct lh_entry *e);
functions.description: Returns 1 if the entry’s key was marked constant (e.g., via JSON_C_OBJECT_ADD_CONSTANT_KEY in insert_w_hash) and thus should not be freed when the entry is freed; otherwise returns 0.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry.
The meaning of the flag is strictly about whether the table’s free function should free the key; it does not imply immutability beyond that.

functions.name: lh_entry_v
functions.description: Returns a non-const pointer to the entry’s value. The value is stored as const internally to ensure linkhash doesn’t modify it.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry.
The caller is responsible for any value memory management policy outside of what the table’s free function handles.

functions.name: lh_entry_set_val
functions.signature: static inline void lh_entry_set_val(struct lh_entry *e, void *newval);
functions.description: Sets a new value pointer on the entry. The caller is responsible for freeing the previous value, if needed.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry that belongs to a live table.
Caller must manage lifetime of the previous value before/after calling, as the function does not free it.
newval may be NULL if the caller intends to store a NULL value; no explicit restriction is documented.

functions.name: lh_entry_next
functions.signature: static inline struct lh_entry *lh_entry_next(const struct lh_entry *e);
functions.description: Returns the next entry in insertion order, or NULL if there is no next entry. Use with lh_table_head() for iteration.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry.
Returned pointer is owned by the table and becomes invalid if the table is modified to remove that entry or the table is freed.

functions.name: lh_entry_prev
functions.signature: static inline struct lh_entry *lh_entry_prev(const struct lh_entry *e);
functions.description: Returns the previous entry in insertion order, or NULL if there is no previous entry.
requirements: e must be a valid pointer to an lh_entry.
Returned pointer is owned by the table and becomes invalid if the table is modified to remove that entry or the table is freed.

functions.name: printbuf_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new dynamic print buffer (printbuf). Use this to obtain a buffer before appending or formatting into it. Free the result with printbuf_free() when done.
requirements: Caller must free the returned buffer with printbuf_free() to avoid memory leaks.
The returned pointer must be checked before use if allocation failures are possible (may be NULL in low-memory situations; not explicitly stated in the header but typical for allocators).

functions.name: printbuf_memappend
functions.signature: int printbuf_memappend(struct printbuf *p, const char *buf, int size)
functions.description: Append size bytes from buf to the print buffer p, growing the internal buffer as needed. This is the underlying append function used by the fast macro and other helpers.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized printbuf pointer created by printbuf_new().
If size > 0, buf should point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
size must be >= 0.
Caller should check the return code for errors (explicitly stated in the header comments).

functions.name: printbuf_memset
functions.signature: int printbuf_memset(struct printbuf *pb, int offset, int charvalue, int len)
functions.description: Set len bytes in the buffer to the byte value charvalue, starting at byte offset offset. The buffer is extended as necessary. If offset is -1, the operation starts at the end of the current data.
requirements: pb must be a valid, initialized printbuf pointer.
len must be >= 0.
offset must be either -1 (to start from the current end) or a valid non-negative byte offset within or just beyond the current buffer; the function extends the buffer as necessary.
charvalue is treated as a byte value (typically 0–255).

functions.name: sprintbuf
functions.description: Formatted print into the print buffer p using a printf-style format string msg and variadic arguments. This is the most expensive way to append string data and should be avoided in hot paths in favor of preformatted data with append helpers.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized printbuf pointer.
msg must be a valid printf-style format string whose format specifiers match the provided variadic arguments.
Due to cost, avoid using in tight loops where performance is critical (recommendation from header comments).

functions.name: printbuf_reset
functions.description: Reset the print buffer to an empty state (typically sets the logical length to 0 and null-terminates). Use this to reuse an existing buffer without freeing and reallocating.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized printbuf pointer.

functions.name: printbuf_free
functions.description: Free a printbuf previously allocated with printbuf_new(), releasing its resources.
requirements: p must be a pointer returned by printbuf_new().
Do not use p after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: printbuf_memappend_fast
functions.signature: macro (no function signature): #define printbuf_memappend_fast(p, bufptr, bufsize)
functions.description: Optimized append macro for adding raw bytes to a printbuf. If the existing buffer has enough free space, it memcpy()s bufsize bytes from bufptr into p->buf at p->bpos, updates bpos, and writes a trailing '\0'. Otherwise it calls printbuf_memappend(p, bufptr, bufsize) to grow the buffer and append. Returns no value; intended as a faster, convenient alternative to calling printbuf_memappend() directly when you don't need to handle its return code.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized pointer to a struct printbuf (e.g., as returned by printbuf_new).
p->buf must point to a valid writable buffer managed by printbuf (implied by proper initialization).
bufptr must be non-NULL and point to at least bufsize readable bytes when bufsize > 0.
bufsize must be >= 0; behavior is meaningful only for bufsize >= 0; negative sizes are invalid.

If insufficient space exists, the macro invokes printbuf_memappend(), whose failure cannot be detected through this macro (no return value). Callers needing error handling must use printbuf_memappend() directly and check its return code.
The appended data is treated as raw bytes; no implicit inclusion of a terminating null beyond the one the macro itself writes after the appended block.

functions.name: printbuf_length
functions.description: Returns the current length (number of valid bytes) stored in a printbuf by expanding to p->bpos. This is a simple accessor macro with no side effects.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized pointer to a struct printbuf.
The returned value reflects the current write position (bpos) and excludes the trailing '\0' maintained by the append operations.

functions.name: printbuf_strappend
functions.signature: macro (no function signature): #define printbuf_strappend(pb, str) printbuf_memappend((pb), _printbuf_check_literal(str), sizeof(str) - 1)
functions.description: Convenience macro to append a string literal to a printbuf without paying the cost of strlen(). At compile time it enforces that str is a string literal via _printbuf_check_literal and passes its known length (excluding the terminating '\0') to printbuf_memappend(). It expands to a call to printbuf_memappend() and thus returns that function’s int result.
requirements: pb must be a valid, initialized pointer to a struct printbuf.
str must be a string literal; passing a non-literal (e.g., char*, std::string.c_str()) will cause a compilation error due to _printbuf_check_literal.
The literal is appended without its terminating '\0' (only its characters are appended); the buffer remains '\0'-terminated by printbuf logic.
Since it expands to printbuf_memappend(), callers should check the returned int for success/failure as defined by printbuf_memappend().

functions.name: json_pointer_get
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_pointer_get(struct json_object *obj, const char *path, struct json_object **res);
functions.description: Retrieve a JSON sub-object from a json-c object tree using an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer path. The returned sub-object is not a newly created object; it is a pointer to an existing node within the provided tree. On success, stores the located json_object pointer at res and returns 0; on error or if the path does not exist, returns a negative value.
requirements: obj must be a valid, initialized json_object tree.
path must be a valid RFC 6901 JSON Pointer string (e.g., "/foo/0/bar").
res must be a non-null pointer to receive the located json_object pointer.
The returned json_object is an existing node in the tree (not newly created).
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates error or not found.

functions.name: json_pointer_getf
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_pointer_getf(struct json_object *obj, struct json_object **res, const char *path_fmt, ...);
functions.description: Variant of json_pointer_get that builds the JSON Pointer path with printf-style formatting. The formatted path is interpreted as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. On success, stores the located json_object pointer at res and returns 0; on error or if the path does not exist, returns a negative value. The returned sub-object points into the existing tree (not newly created).
requirements: obj must be a valid, initialized json_object tree.
res must be a non-null pointer to receive the located json_object pointer.
path_fmt must be a non-null printf-style format string for an RFC 6901 path.
The variable arguments must match path_fmt as in printf; escape percent signs with "%%" where needed.
The formatted path must be a valid RFC 6901 JSON Pointer string.
Observe general printf-style format string safety considerations.
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates error or not found.

functions.name: json_pointer_set
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_pointer_set(struct json_object **obj, const char *path, struct json_object *value);
functions.description: Set or replace the JSON value within the json-c object tree at the location designated by an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer path. If path is the empty string (""), the entire object referenced by *obj is replaced by value; the previous *obj has its refcount decremented. For non-empty paths, ownership of value is transferred into *obj via json_object_object_add/json_object_array_put_idx. On success returns 0; on error or if the path cannot be resolved/created, returns a negative value.
requirements: obj must be a non-null pointer to a json_object* (double pointer), because an empty path may replace the root object.
path must be a valid RFC 6901 JSON Pointer string; the empty string is allowed and replaces the entire object.
value must be a valid json_object to be inserted/set.
On empty path: the object currently at *obj will have its refcount decremented via json_object_put(), and *obj will be assigned to value.
On non-empty paths: ownership of value is transferred into *obj via json_object_object_add()/json_object_array_put_idx().
Do not decrement value’s refcount on success; only decrement value’s refcount if the function returns a negative value (indicating it was not set).
json_pointer_set does not increment any refcounts (aside from the single decrement of the old root object in the empty-path case).
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates error or not found.

functions.name: json_pointer_setf
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_pointer_setf(struct json_object **obj, struct json_object *value, const char *path_fmt, ...);
functions.description: Variant of json_pointer_set that builds the RFC 6901 path using a printf-style format string and arguments. If the formatted path is empty (""), replaces the entire object at *obj with value, decrementing the previous object’s refcount. For non-empty paths, transfers ownership of value into *obj. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: obj must be a non-null pointer to a json_object* (double pointer), because an empty path may replace the root object.
value must be a valid json_object to be inserted/set.
path_fmt must be a non-null printf-style format string that produces an RFC 6901 path; escape percent signs with "%%" as in printf.
The variable arguments must match path_fmt as in printf; observe standard printf-format security considerations.
On empty formatted path: the object currently at *obj will have its refcount decremented via json_object_put(), and *obj will be assigned to value.
On non-empty paths: ownership of value is transferred into *obj via json_object_object_add()/json_object_array_put_idx().
Do not decrement value’s refcount on success; only decrement value’s refcount if the function returns a negative value (indicating it was not set).
json_pointer_setf does not increment any refcounts (aside from the single decrement of the old root object in the empty-path case).
Check the return value: 0 indicates success; a negative value indicates error or not found.

functions.name: json_patch_apply
functions.signature: JSON_EXPORT int json_patch_apply(struct json_object *copy_from, struct json_object *patch, struct json_object **base, struct json_patch_error *patch_error);
functions.description: Applies a JSON Patch (RFC 6902) to a JSON-C object. The patch must be a json_type_array of operations. The function modifies *base in place if *base is non-NULL, or, if *base is NULL, it deep-copies copy_from into *base first and then applies the patch. Returns 0 on complete success; a negative value on failure, optionally filling patch_error with details (errno-style code, failing operation index, and a static error message). Typical usage: pass either an existing base object to be patched (with copy_from == NULL), or pass a source object in copy_from and a pointer to a NULL *base to have a new, patchable copy created.
requirements: patch must be a non-NULL struct json_object representing a JSON array (json_type_array) of RFC 6902 operations.
base must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct json_object* (i.e., you must pass the address of a json_object*).
Exactly one of *base or copy_from must be non-NULL at call time: if *base is non-NULL then copy_from must be NULL; if *base is NULL then copy_from must be non-NULL.

If *base is NULL on entry, the function will allocate a deep copy of copy_from into *base via json_object_deep_copy(); the caller must later free *base using json_object_put(), even if the function ultimately fails.
On error (negative return), callers should check patch_error (if non-NULL) for details; json_patch_error.errmsg points to static storage and must not be freed by the caller.
json_patch_error.patch_failure_idx (if set) indicates the zero-based index of the failing operation in the patch array, or SIZE_T_MAX for overall (non-operation-specific) errors.

The function may return errno-style codes in json_patch_error.errno_code such as ENOENT (path not found), EINVAL (invalid operation/path), ENOMEM (allocation failure), and EFAULT (invalid arguments to json_patch_apply).
Callers must not assume ownership transfer of patch or copy_from; only *base allocation is managed by the function when *base is NULL on entry.
The function modifies *base in place when *base is non-NULL; callers should not rely on implicit immutability of the input object.
